title: Get a User's Gmail Message
knowledge:
# Get a User's Gmail Message

## Prerequisites

- Must have access to the user’s Gmail mailbox with an appropriate Gmail scope (see **Notes**).

## Method

`GET`

## URL

`https://gmail.googleapis.com/gmail/v1/users/{{userId}}/messages/{{id}}`

## Headers

```json
{
  "Accept": "application/json"
}
```

## Description

Gets a specific Gmail message by message ID. You can control how much of the message is returned using the `format` query parameter (e.g., minimal metadata, full parsed payload, raw RFC 2822 content, or headers-only metadata).

## Enforcement Rules

- The `userId` path parameter **must always be present**.
- If the user provides a `userId`, use that value directly.
- If the user does **not** provide a `userId`, default it explicitly to `"me"`.
- Always construct the path as `/gmail/v1/users/{{userId}}/messages/{{id}}`, where `{{userId}}` is a **non-empty string**.
- Do **not** call the API with a missing or empty `userId` (e.g., avoid `/gmail/v1/users//messages/{{id}}`).
- The `id` path parameter **must always be present** and **non-empty**.
- When executing the action, ensure to send **Path Parameters** in the URL and **not** in the body.
- When executing the action, ensure to send **Query Parameters** in the URL as query parameters and **not** in the body.

### Valid Examples

```http
/gmail/v1/users/me/messages/186a7c2d3f9a1b2c
/gmail/v1/users/user@example.com/messages/186a7c2d3f9a1b2c
```

### Invalid Examples

```http
/gmail/v1/users//messages/186a7c2d3f9a1b2c
/gmail/v1/users/me/messages/
/gmail/v1/users/me/messages
```

## Required Path Parameters

| Parameter | Type   | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| `userId` | string | The user's email address. The special value `me` can be used to indicate the authenticated user. Default: `me`. |
| `id`     | string | The ID of the message to retrieve. This ID is usually retrieved using `messages.list`. The ID is also contained in results when a message is inserted (`messages.insert`) or imported (`messages.import`). |

## Optional Query Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| `format` | string | The format to return the message in. Default: `full`. Possible values: `minimal` (only message ID and labels), `full` (full message data with body parsed in `payload`; `raw` not used), `raw` (full message data with body in `raw` as base64url; `payload` not used), `metadata` (only message ID, labels, and headers). Note: `full`/`raw` cannot be used when accessing the API using the `gmail.metadata` scope. |
| `metadataHeaders` | string (repeated) | When given and `format` is `METADATA`, only include headers specified. (Repeat the query parameter to specify multiple headers.) |

## Response

### Success Response (200 OK)

```json
{
  "id": "186a7c2d3f9a1b2c",
  "threadId": "186a7c2c1a0b9d8e",
  "labelIds": ["INBOX", "UNREAD"],
  "snippet": "A short part of the message text.",
  "internalDate": "1710000000000",
  "sizeEstimate": 52341,
  "historyId": "987654321",
  "payload": {
    "partId": "",
    "mimeType": "multipart/alternative",
    "filename": "",
    "headers": [
      { "name": "From", "value": "Sender <sender@example.com>" },
      { "name": "To", "value": "user@example.com" },
      { "name": "Subject", "value": "Example subject" },
      { "name": "Date", "value": "Mon, 10 Mar 2025 10:00:00 +0000" }
    ],
    "body": {
      "size": 0
    },
    "parts": [
      {
        "partId": "0",
        "mimeType": "text/plain",
        "filename": "",
        "headers": [{ "name": "Content-Type", "value": "text/plain; charset=UTF-8" }],
        "body": {
          "size": 120,
          "data": "VGhpcyBpcyBhIHBsYWluIHRleHQgYm9keS4"
        }
      },
      {
        "partId": "1",
        "mimeType": "text/html",
        "filename": "",
        "headers": [{ "name": "Content-Type", "value": "text/html; charset=UTF-8" }],
        "body": {
          "size": 240,
          "data": "PGRpdj5UaGlzIGlzIGFuIEhUTUwgYm9keS48L2Rpdj4"
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

### Error Responses

The scraped content did not provide explicit error response bodies for this endpoint.

## Response Fields

| Field | Type | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| `id` | string | The immutable ID of the message. |
| `threadId` | string | The ID of the thread the message belongs to. To add a message/draft to a thread, criteria include matching `threadId`, compliant `References`/`In-Reply-To` headers, and matching `Subject`. |
| `labelIds` | array[string] | List of IDs of labels applied to this message. |
| `snippet` | string | A short part of the message text. |
| `internalDate` | string (int64) | Internal message creation timestamp (epoch ms) used for ordering. |
| `sizeEstimate` | integer (int32) | Estimated size in bytes of the message. |
| `historyId` | string (uint64) | The ID of the last history record that modified this message. |
| `payload` | object | A single MIME message part (parsed content when `format=full` or `metadata`). |
| `payload.partId` | string | The immutable ID of the message part. |
| `payload.mimeType` | string | The MIME type of the message part. |
| `payload.filename` | string | Filename of the attachment (only present if this part represents an attachment). |
| `payload.headers` | array[object] | Headers on this message part (top-level includes standard RFC 2822 headers like `To`, `From`, `Subject`). |
| `payload.headers[].name` | string | Header name before the `:` separator (e.g., `To`). |
| `payload.headers[].value` | string | Header value after the `:` separator (e.g., `someuser@example.com`). |
| `payload.body` | object | The body of a single MIME message part. |
| `payload.body.size` | integer (int32) | Number of bytes for the message part data (encoding notwithstanding). |
| `payload.body.data` | string | Body data as a base64url encoded string. May be empty for container parts or when content is provided as an attachment. |
| `payload.body.attachmentId` | string | If present, ID of an external attachment retrievable via `messages.attachments.get`. |
| `payload.parts` | array | Child MIME parts (applies to container parts like `multipart/*`). |
| `raw` | string | Entire email message in RFC 2822 format, base64url encoded. Returned when `format=RAW` is supplied. |
| `classificationLabelValues` | array[object] | Classification Label values on the message (Google Workspace accounts only). |
| `classificationLabelValues[].labelId` | string | Required. Canonical or raw alphanumeric classification label ID (maps to Google Drive Labels API). |
| `classificationLabelValues[].fields` | array[object] | Field values for the given classification label ID. |
| `classificationLabelValues[].fields[].fieldId` | string | Required. Field ID for the Classification Label Value. |
| `classificationLabelValues[].fields[].selection` | string | Selection choice ID (only if the field type is `SELECTION`). |

## Sample Request

```bash
curl -i --location --request GET \
  'https://gmail.googleapis.com/gmail/v1/users/me/messages/186a7c2d3f9a1b2c?format=full' \
  --header 'Accept: application/json'
```

## Example Usage

### Example 1: Get minimal message info (ID + labels)

```bash
curl -sS --location \
  'https://gmail.googleapis.com/gmail/v1/users/me/messages/186a7c2d3f9a1b2c?format=minimal' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

### Example 2: Get raw RFC 2822 message (base64url encoded)

```bash
curl -sS --location \
  'https://gmail.googleapis.com/gmail/v1/users/me/messages/186a7c2d3f9a1b2c?format=raw' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

### Example 3: Get only specific headers (metadata)

```bash
curl -sS --location \
  'https://gmail.googleapis.com/gmail/v1/users/me/messages/186a7c2d3f9a1b2c?format=metadata&metadataHeaders=From&metadataHeaders=To&metadataHeaders=Subject' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

## Behavior

1. Validates `userId` and message `id`.
2. Retrieves the message.
3. Shapes the response based on `format`:
   - `full`: parsed content in `payload`
   - `raw`: raw content in `raw` (base64url); `payload` not used
   - `metadata`: message ID, labels, and headers (optionally filtered by `metadataHeaders`)
   - `minimal`: message ID and labels only

## Notes

- Scopes listed for this endpoint include:
  - `https://mail.google.com/`
  - `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.readonly`
  - `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.modify`
  - `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.metadata`
  - `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.addons.current.message.*` (as shown in the scraped content)
- `format=full` and `format=raw` cannot be used when accessing the API using the `gmail.metadata` scope (per scraped description).
- `metadataHeaders` is a **repeated** query parameter (specify it multiple times to request multiple headers).

## Gotchas

- `metadataHeaders` only applies when using metadata format (documented as `format` is `METADATA`); using it with other formats may not have the intended effect.
- If a MIME part’s `body.attachmentId` is present, the content may need to be fetched separately via `messages.attachments.get` rather than using `body.data`.

## Recipe — Extract headers and decode the body

For `format=full` the response is a MIME tree. To get the data agents usually want:

- **Envelope headers (From/To/Cc/Subject/Date):** search `payload.headers[]` for the matching `name` value. The top-level `payload.headers` array contains the RFC 2822 headers; sub-parts only carry MIME headers like `Content-Type`.
- **Body text:**
  - If `payload.mimeType` starts with `text/` and `payload.body.data` is set: base64url-decode `payload.body.data` (replace `-` → `+`, `_` → `/`, pad with `=` to a multiple of 4, then base64-decode).
  - Otherwise walk `payload.parts[]` recursively and pick the part whose `mimeType` is `text/plain` (preferred) or `text/html`. Base64url-decode that part's `body.data` the same way.
- **Attachments:** parts where `body.attachmentId` is set (and `body.data` is empty). Fetch each via **Get a Gmail Message Attachment** (`conn_mod_def::GJ3ocG2ED_w::LGrrJyM-QFmKBaHwvMWwzQ`) using `messageId` + the part's `attachmentId`.

If the caller only needs envelope fields (From/To/Subject/Date), pass `format=metadata` with `metadataHeaders` — the response is ~1 KB instead of the typical 50–200 KB of `format=full`, and skips the base64url decoding entirely.
